messages:
incident-bot: ALERT 1966543210 - GPU pool 'east-prod-pool-1' queue depth > 90% (threshold 60%). Auto-scale attempted but blocked by scale limit. Tag: severity=high

pagerduty: @priya on-call (primary) alert acknowledged :rotating_light:

priya: seeing lots of 429s from frontend metrics. thanks for the ping. jumping in, collecting quick context. is this a pure capacity exhaust or a config change?

sam: looks like autoscaler tried to add nodes but rejected by quota: 
```
AutoscaleEvent: desired=64, max_allowed=50, result=cap_reached
GPUQuotaCheck: allowed=50, current=50
```
queue growth is steady; token-serving latency spiked ~3x in last 6m.

li: cpu/gpu utilization per-node is ~85-95% so pool is effectively saturated. also seeing a big drop in batchcache hit rate (prefix-cache hit-rate from ~82% -> ~12%) which would blow up per-request work.

emma: omg prefix cache miss storm. any recent rollout touching continuous-batching or cache TTLs?

jason: pushed a config change 14m ago to tweak continuous batching windows and prefix-cache TTL as an experiment (PR #2345). rollout was a canary then auto-promote. I reverted the commit on canary just now but prod still has new config.

priya: ok that explains correlation. if prefix cache misses are high, more KV/cache recompute and bigger batch sizes -> slower per-token throughput -> backlog -> autoscale tries to catch up -> hits scale cap. we need triage steps: 
1) reduce incoming load (rate-limit non-critical routes)
2) emergency rollback of batching/cache config in prod
3) increase reserved capacity (if possible) or raise autoscale cap
4) short-term fallback model for high qps customers

sam: on (1) adding temporary 20% rate limit on non-paid routes, pushing rule to ingress. doing now: 
```
kubectl apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: networking/v1
kind: IngressPolicy
metadata:
  name: temp-rate-limit-nonpaid
spec:
  routes:
  - match: "/v1/generate*"
    header: "x-plan"
    value: "free"
    limit: 20%
EOF
```

deploy-bot: deploy queued: ingresspolicy/temp-rate-limit-nonpaid -> rollout started

deploy-bot: deploy succeeded: ingresspolicy/temp-rate-limit-nonpaid (1m)

li: rate limit applied, client qps dropped ~18% within 60s. queue growth slowed but still > steady state.

priya: good. sam can you attempt rollback of batch/cache config to last-known-good? jason can you confirm commit id?

jason: yes last-known-good is commit abc123 (before PR #2345). I'm preparing rollback. note: the change touched two things: continuousBatch.windowMs: 50->120 and prefixCache.ttlSecs: 300->20. the low TTL is likely causing cache churn.

sam: prepping rollback now. caution: changing batching window back down will reduce single-request latency but might increase token cost. fine tradeoff during incident.

sam: rollback command:
```
redwoodctl config apply --pool east-prod-pool-1 --from-commit abc123 --components continuousBatch,prefixCache
```
Running...

deploy-bot: config apply started: redwoodctl config apply --pool east-prod-pool-1 --from-commit abc123 -> waiting for rollout

deploy-bot: config apply succeeded (2m): continuousBatch.windowMs=50, prefixCache.ttlSecs=300

li: cache hit-rate climbing back up, now ~68% after ~90s. per-node throughput improving. queue depth trending down.

priya: excellent. next: autoscale cap still at 50 so if we see another surge we may fail again. can we temporarily bump quota to 80 for east-prod-pool-1? who owns infra quota?

jason: cloud quota requests typically take time but we have emergency soft limits within org: sam can increase pool max via infra arena for 30m window. sam?

sam: on it. bumping pool max to 80, keeping aggressive cooldowns. command:
```
redwoodctl pools update east-prod-pool-1 --max-nodes 80 --emergency-ttl 1800
```
Done.

sam: autoscaler noticed new cap, desired scaled to 72, nodes coming up. health checks failing for a couple of nodes (init container OOM) - investigating.

li: the node OOMs look like image cache eviction thrash from rollout combined with high startup concurrency. lowering parallel node startup to 4. applying patch.

sam: parallel startup limited; new nodes stabilized. overall available GPUs up to 68. queue dropping steadily, 429 rate back down to baseline for most customers.

emma: customer impact — during the peak window (approx 16:10-16:32 UTC) some customers saw elevated latency and 429s. ACME-Corp (account-acme) experienced 30% request errors for ~18 minutes. We're preparing post-incident note.

priya: good, let's assemble timeline and action items for postmortem. immediate action items: 
- jason to revert config change permanently or gate it behind feature flag (done as emergency rollback)
- sam to run a bounded experiment for rollout cadence and node startup parallelism (3 days)
- infra to provision higher soft limit for east-prod region and codify emergency quota bump runbook (owner: jason)
- observability: add alert for prefix-cache-hit-rate drop below 60% to correlate with queue depth (owner: li)
- product: notify affected customers, include mitigation and ETA for follow-up (owner: emma)

jason: I'll open PR to add a canary-only flag on the batching experiment and add a guard so low TTLs can't be promoted automatically.

li: I'll add alert + dashboard: "prefix_cache_hit_rate" and a synthetic that watches a sample prompt set for degrade.

sam: followup: need to create an automated rollback policy when autoscaler fails to progress due to cap and queues grow beyond X for Y minutes. add to runbook.

deploy-bot: incident-bot note: severity downgraded to medium at 1966543580 after queue < 40% and customer errors <= baseline.

priya: handing off to oncall rotation for post-incident follow-up. assigning pagerduty postmortem to jason + li + emma. I'll write the summary: 
```
Summary: 14:10-14:32 incident in east-prod caused by config drift from PR #2345 which reduced prefix-cache TTL and increased batching window. Result: cache miss storm -> reduced throughput -> autoscaler hit configured max -> queue growth and throttles. Mitigations: ingress rate-limit, rollback to abc123, emergency pool cap bump, controlled node startup. Impact: elevated latency and 429s for subset of customers (notably account-acme). Action items: see list above.
```

oncall-rota-bot: @jason assigned to postmortem doc (due 72h).

priya: thanks everyone. leaving notes in incident tracker and will ping customer ops to notify accounts. I'll close the live thread once postmortem is filed.

oncall-rota-bot: incident closed (live) 1966543660 - followups assigned

sam: logging final metrics snapshot for PostMortem: 
```
queue_depth_peak: 9200
queue_depth_end: 420
prefix_cache_hit_peak_low: 12%
prefix_cache_hit_post_rollback: 72%
autoscale_max_before: 50
autoscale_max_after: 80
customer_error_peak: 12% (global), 30% (account-acme)
```

emma: drafting customer-facing note now. will post to #customer-success and send targeted email to impacted accounts.

priya: good work. closing thread for live mitigation. follow-ups in postmortem channel. :white_check_mark:
